candidates.summary: iconHeadingIDTransformer skips empty ATX headings (Lines().Len()==0) and never registers their goldmark id in the fresh linearIDs, so a later heading slugging to "heading" gets a duplicate id
candidates.failure_scenario:
A realm page with an empty heading `##` and any heading carrying an icon: `##

## <gno-icon name="star" label="Top" />` renders two <h2 id="heading">; `##

## Heading

## <gno-icon name="star" /> A` renders ids [heading heading a] where the same doc without the icon gives [heading heading-1]. The TOC entry and any #heading anchor for the second heading jump to the empty one, and the DOM carries duplicate ids. Fix: ids.Put the kept id of a heading with no lines, or regenerate it with ids.Generate(nil, ast.KindHeading).

candidates.summary: aloneInNamedParent's heading-wide walk marks icons nested in a link as hintDone with hint=false, so an icon-only link inside a heading that has an earlier unlabeled icon never gets its add-label hint
candidates.failure_scenario: `## <gno-icon name="star" /> Title [<gno-icon name="star" />](/r/x)`: the first icon's parent is the heading; its walk descends into the link, sets c.hintDone=true on the link's icon and only assigns first.hint, so the link's icon returns hint=false and no `<!-- gno-icon: alone in a link or heading ... -->` is written, although the link has no accessible name. `## Title [<gno-icon name="star" />](/r/x)` (no earlier icon) does get the hint. Fix: in the walk, return WalkSkipChildren on a nested namedByContent node other than parent.
candidates.verify_by: cd gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/markdown && cp <repro> zz_b3_hint_test.go && go test -count=1 -run TestB3LinkHintLostInsideHeading -v .
candidates.evidence: control `## Title [<gno-icon name="star" />](/r/x)` contains the hint; probes log: an icon-only link inside a heading got no hint: "## <gno-icon name=\"star\" /> Title [<gno-icon name=\"star\" />](/r/x)\n" and the two-link variant; --- FAIL: TestB3LinkHintLostInsideHeading

candidates.summary: FuzzIconRender's event-handler oracle flags any labeled icon whose label contains a word starting with "on", a false positive
candidates.failure_scenario: Input `<gno-icon name="star" label="turn on" />` renders `<svg class="gno-icon" ... role="img" aria-label="turn on">`; the tag before the first '>' contains " on", so t.Fatalf("event handler in ...") fires on a safe render under `go test -fuzz`. Check for an attribute name instead (e.g. a regexp on `\s on[a-z]+=` outside the quoted aria-label).

candidates.summary: An unquoted name directly followed by `/>` gets the "write it self-closing" hint although the author wrote `/>`
candidates.failure_scenario: `<gno-icon name=star/> x` renders `<!-- gno-icon: write it self-closing, <gno-icon name="…" /> -->`: scanGnoTag (utils.go:105, shared byte-for-byte with #6298 and #6299) reads the unquoted value as `star/`, HTML-correct, so SelfClosing is false and the hint tells the author to do what they did. Changing scanGnoTag would break `href=/r/x/` in the sibling PRs, so the fix belongs in the hint: say to add a space or quote the name when n.Name ends in '/'.

candidates.summary: The transformer regenerates every heading id from a hardcoded newLinearIDs(), ignoring pc.IDs() and overwriting explicit ids, for any consumer of the exported ExtIcons/NewGnoExtension that enables parser.WithAttribute
candidates.failure_scenario: Latent: a goldmark built with parser.WithAttribute() and NewGnoExtension parses `## Intro {#custom}` and one `## <gno-icon name="star" /> A`; the transformer finds an id on every heading and replaces `custom` with `intro`, and a caller's own parser.WithIDs generator is bypassed. In-tree the realm renderer has no WithAttribute (render_config.go:36) and documentationGM (render.go:107) has no GnoExtension, so nothing ships it today.
